text: Differentiating common causes of piglet/pig diarrhea by age and appearance: E. coli in newborn piglets (before 5 days) — yellow, creamy, mucus-containing diarrhea, wet/dirty anus and tail, later dehydration; treat by injecting all littermates with Colistin+Ampicillin morning and evening, and give the sow TMP+Sulfa to reduce E. coli in her milk; prevent by ensuring colostrum intake right after birth (antibody protection) and avoiding cold/drafts (a cold abdomen favors E. coli multiplication) with a warm nest. Coccidiosis (7–21 days old) — yellow-to-grey-green diarrhea, creamy-to-doughy consistency, piglets waste away but rarely die; treatment (sulfadimidine or sulfadimethoxine) has limited success, so prevention (a single oral Toltrazuril dose 3 days after birth) is much more effective. Bloody diarrhea from Clostridium — rapid onset (1–7 days old) of rotten-smelling, often blood-colored diarrhea, with many deaths, common in scavenging piglets; treat with Amoxicillin, ideally given orally. E. coli in weaned piglets (usually 5–7 days post-weaning) — very watery to pasty consistency, color varies (grey-white, yellow, green — color itself isn't diagnostic, and there's no blood/mucus), dehydration with rapid weight loss; treat with Colistin, TMP+Sulfa, Gentamicin, or Enrofloxacin; prevent with a warm environment right after weaning, dedicated post-weaning commercial feed suited to the piglet's still-adapting digestion, and mixing Colistin into feed for the first week post-weaning. Grey diarrhea/Ileitis (fattening pigs or sows) — chronic, watery, grey, sloppy diarrhea with poor condition, or an acute bloody form with anemia (pale conjunctiva); treat with Tylosin, Tylosin+Gentamicin, or Tiamulin. Salmonellosis (often secondary to CSF) — foul-smelling watery diarrhea (sometimes bloody), respiratory distress and coughing, red skin with blue tail/ears, jaundice from liver damage; treatment (TMP+Sulfa or Enrofloxacin) is difficult; vaccination is not useful — prevention relies on hygiene, disinfection, and rodent control.
